## 1. Introduction

Influenza A virus (IAV) infection triggers a complex transcriptomic response 
in host tissues. While much research has focused on peripheral immune responses, 
the effects of influenza infection on the central nervous system (CNS) remain 
less well understood. This project investigates transcriptomic changes in mouse 
cerebellum tissue following Influenza A infection at two time points (Day 4 and 
Day 8 post-infection) compared to non-infected controls.

The dataset used is GSE96870, which contains paired-end RNA-seq data from 
9 mouse cerebellum samples: 3 non-infected controls (Day 0), 3 infected at 
Day 4, and 3 infected at Day 8 post-infection.

## 2. Methods

### 2.1 Data Acquisition
Raw RNA-seq data was downloaded from NCBI SRA using `prefetch` and converted 
to FASTQ format using `fastq-dump` (SRA Toolkit v3.4.1). The dataset comprises 
9 paired-end samples (SRR5364316, SRR5364317, SRR5364322, SRR5364318, 
SRR5364319, SRR5364323, SRR5364321, SRR5364325, SRR5364330).

### 2.2 Quality Control
Raw reads were assessed using FastQC. All samples showed high quality scores 
(Phred > 30) across read lengths with minimal adapter contamination, indicating 
no trimming was necessary.

### 2.3 Alignment
Reads were aligned to the Mus musculus reference genome (GRCm39, Ensembl 
release 116) using HISAT2. All samples achieved 100% overall alignment rates,
confirming high-quality alignments.

### 2.4 Read Counting
Read counts were generated using featureCounts with the GRCm39 GTF annotation 
file. Count matrices were merged across all 9 samples for downstream analysis.

### 2.5 Differential Expression Analysis
Differential expression analysis was performed using DESeq2 in R. Three 
comparisons were made:
- Flu4 vs Control (Day 4 infected vs non-infected)
- Flu8 vs Control (Day 8 infected vs non-infected)
- Flu8 vs Flu4 (Day 8 vs Day 4 infected)

Genes with |log2FoldChange| > 1 and adjusted p-value < 0.05 were considered 
significant. LFC shrinkage was applied using the `ashr` method.

### 2.6 Pathway Enrichment Analysis
GO Biological Process and KEGG pathway enrichment analyses were performed using 
`clusterProfiler` with the `org.Mm.eg.db` annotation database.

## 3. Results

### 3.1 Principal Component Analysis

```{r pca, echo=FALSE, fig.cap="PCA of VST-transformed counts"}
knitr::include_graphics("Results/Figures/PCA_plot.png")
```

The PCA plot shows partial separation between conditions, with some variability 
between replicates, potentially reflecting biological heterogeneity and sex 
differences between samples.

### 3.2 Sample Distance Heatmap

```{r sample_dist, echo=FALSE, fig.cap="Sample Distance Heatmap"}
knitr::include_graphics("Results/Figures/sample_distance_heatmap.png")
```

### 3.3 Differential Expression Results

A summary of differentially expressed genes (|log2FC| > 1, padj < 0.05) 
across all three comparisons:

| Comparison | Total DEGs |
|------------|-----------|
| Flu4 vs Control | 24 |
| Flu8 vs Control | 655 |
| Flu8 vs Flu4 | 212 |

The relatively few DEGs at Day 4 suggests the immune response is still 
developing, while the dramatic increase at Day 8 reflects a full-scale 
transcriptomic response to influenza infection.

|---------|-------------|-----------------|

| GO:0034341 | Response to type II interferon | 6.32e-05 |
| GO:0035458 | Cellular response to interferon-beta | 1.63e-04 |
| GO:0071346 | Cellular response to type II interferon | 1.40e-03 |
| GO:0009636 | Response to toxic substance | 4.55e-03 |

## 4. Discussion

This analysis reveals a time-dependent transcriptomic response to Influenza A 
infection in mouse cerebellum. The minimal DEGs at Day 4 (n=24) compared to 
Day 8 (n=655) suggests the immune response escalates significantly between 
these time points.

The dominant GO enrichment terms — interferon response pathways — are 
consistent with known antiviral immunity. Both type I (interferon-beta) and 
type II (interferon-gamma) interferon response pathways were significantly 
enriched, highlighting the robust innate immune activation in cerebellar tissue 
during influenza infection.

The KEGG enrichment of lipid metabolism pathways (ether lipid, linolenic acid, 
and linoleic acid metabolism) is biologically relevant, as influenza viruses 
are known to exploit host lipid metabolism for viral envelope assembly and 
replication. These findings suggest that even in CNS tissue, influenza 
infection significantly disrupts lipid homeostasis.

The partial clustering in PCA may reflect the mixed sex composition of the 
dataset (male and female mice), which could contribute to transcriptomic 
variability independent of infection status.
